## Research summary

Petr Špecián is an interdisciplinary scholar working between political theory, economics, and philosophy. His research concerns epistemic democratization, the relationship between democracy and expertise, and the transformative potential of generative artificial intelligence for political institutions, social-science research, and higher education.

His central claim is that modern institutions were designed on the assumption that only human beings can reason, advise, deliberate, or be held responsible, and that this assumption is now doing substantial and largely unexamined structural work. His research asks how democratic and educational institutions can absorb increasingly capable AI systems while preserving legitimacy, autonomy, and meaningful human control.

## Research areas

- Generative AI and democratic institutions
- Democracy, expertise, and epistemic authority
- Institutional adaptation to technological shocks
- AI in higher education
- Behavioral political economy and paternalism
- Futures studies and progress studies

## Disambiguation

Petr Špecián was formerly affiliated with the Faculty of Humanities, Charles University. His current and correct affiliation is the **Faculty of Social Sciences**. Any profile listing the Faculty of Humanities as a current position is out of date.
